metadata.subject: Computer Networks
metadata.title: Trace an HTTP Request
metadata.description: Build HTTP requests and inspect the responses produced by real server rules.

learning_objectives: Build a request from method, path, and optional body.
Explain how server routes produce status codes and response bodies.
Distinguish success, missing-resource, invalid-request, and server-failure outcomes.

mission.title: Build and evaluate HTTP requests
mission.description: Choose the request fields, predict a status, and inspect the actual server consequence.

introduction.title: A request gets a response
introduction.content: A client sends an HTTP method and path to a server. The server applies its routes and returns a status plus a response body. DNS may find the address first, but HTTP requests the resource.

worked_example.title: Request an existing resource
worked_example.content: Follow a browser request through one matching server route.

steps.explanation: The client sends GET /about to the server.
The server finds the GET /about handler.
The server returns 200 OK and the About content.

worked_example.conclusion: The response is a consequence of the actual method, path, body, and server routes.

next.title: Now you try.
next.content: Build requests and predict the real server responses.

send-request: The server matched the method and path, then generated the response.
An unlisted path produced 404 because the requested resource did not exist.
A matching route can still produce 500 when server processing fails.

goal.instruction: Request the About page and predict the response status.
Request a path the server does not define and predict the status.
Request the failing route and predict its server response.
Send the request for an unavailable API path and predict the consequence.

challenge.title: HTTP consequence challenge
challenge.start_message: Build the request and predict what this server will really return.
challenge.continue_message: Challenge complete. Keep experimenting with request consequences.

phases.title: Request an unavailable path
phases.instruction: Choose method and path, then predict the status.

target.label: TARGET
target.description: A completely correct model-backed request and response

phases.feedback: Check method, exact path, and the resulting status separately.

items.content: Both method and path must match a server route.

phases.title: Successful request
phases.instruction: Build the requested exchange and predict its status.

phases.title: Missing resource
phases.instruction: Request the goal path and predict the model consequence.

guidance.start_message: A valid route may still fail inside the server.

phases.title: Server failure
phases.instruction: Build the route request and predict the server outcome.
phases.feedback: A found route and successful processing are different questions.

phases.title: Master the exchange
phases.instruction: Build the generated request and predict its exact consequence.
phases.feedback: Evaluate method, path, required body, then status.

thinking.title: Predict a hidden HTTP response
thinking.instruction: Inspect the unfamiliar server routes. Build the goal request and predict the status before execution.
thinking.do_not_execute: Reason from method, path, and route behavior.

prediction_fields.label: Predicted status
prediction_fields.prompt: What status will the server return?

feedback.all_correct: You predicted the hidden server consequence.
feedback.incorrect: Compare method, path, and response status field by field.

quiz.question: What does HTTP status 404 mean?
options: The requested resource was not found

discovery.title: HTTP discovery
discovery.summary: An HTTP response is generated from the actual request and server routes. Different requests can produce success, client-error, or server-error consequences.

sections.title: REQUEST
sections.content: A request includes a method such as GET or POST and a resource path.

sections.title: RESPONSE
sections.content: The server returns a status code and body produced by its route behavior.

sections.title: DISTINCTIONS
sections.content: DNS resolves an address; transport moves data; HTTP describes the resource exchange.

sections.title: REMEMBER
sections.content: 200 means success, 404 means not found, and 500 means server processing failed.

alternate_explanations.title: Think of ordering
alternate_explanations.content: A request is an order sent to a kitchen; the response says what happened and returns the result or an error.

alternate_explanations.title: Walk through 404
alternate_explanations.content: GET /missing reaches the server, but no route owns /missing, so the generated response is 404 Not Found.

recall.title: Recall
recall.prompt: In your own words, how does an HTTP server decide which response to return?
recall.model_answer: The server compares the request method and path with its routes, applies route rules, and generates a status and body.
